extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to Nature (prospective Nature contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and editorial criteria for preparing and submitting an original research Article to Nature, and for understanding how manuscripts are handled from submission through acceptance, revision, production and publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report original scientific research
rubrics_metrics.description: The main results and conclusions must not have been published or submitted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles must report original scientific research. Authors submit on the understanding that they agree to Nature's publication policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding scientific importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be of outstanding scientific importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of the core criteria for publication in Nature; Nature is highly selective (only about 8% acceptance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest to an interdisciplinary readership
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must reach a conclusion of interest to an interdisciplinary readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature's editors judge whether a paper is likely to interest readers outside its immediate field; significance to a broad readership is an editorial judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large dataset paper standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Large dataset papers should aim to either report a fully comprehensive data set (defined by complete and extensive validation) or provide significant technical advance or scientific insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such papers should either be a fully comprehensive dataset with extensive validation, or offer significant technical advance or insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical paper standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that make solely technical advances will be considered when the technique reported will have significant impacts on communities of fellow researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical advances are considered if they will significantly impact research communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic paper standard
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of novel mechanistic insight, therapeutic papers will be considered if the therapeutic effect reported will provide significant impact on an important disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therapeutic findings without new mechanism can be considered provided the effect has significant clinical/disease impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial triage for peer review: novelty and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The criteria for a paper to be sent for peer-review are that the results seem novel, arresting (illuminating, unexpected or surprising), and that the work described has both immediate and far-reaching implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This initial judgement is not a reflection on technical validity or importance to specialists; it is about novelty, being 'arresting', and broad implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability and explanation for nonspecialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors pay special attention to the readability of submitted material and encourage authors in highly technical disciplines to provide a slightly longer summary paragraph that describes clearly the basic background and how the new results have affected the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to include clear summary paragraphs and a simple schematic summarizing the main conclusion (which can be published as Supplementary Information) to help nonspecialist readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting and submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should use the formatting guide to ensure level, length and format (layout of figures, tables and Supplementary Information) conform with Nature's requirements, and submit via the online manuscript submission system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhering to the formatting guide at submission and each revision stage reduces delays. Follow formatting guidance for figures/tables/Supplementary Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter purpose and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The cover letter is optional but an excellent opportunity to briefly discuss the importance of the submitted work and why it is appropriate for the journal; avoid repeating abstract/introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover letter is not shared with referees and should be used for confidential information (conflicts of interest, related work in press/submitted elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees are chosen for independence from the authors and their institutions; ability to evaluate the technical aspects of the paper fully and fairly; currently or recently assessing related submissions; and availability to assess the manuscript within the requested time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most papers sent to two or three referees; choice made by handling editor, sometimes in consultation with related-field editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: What an ideal referee report should state
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal referee's report indicates who will be interested in the new results and why, and any technical failings that need to be addressed before the authors' case is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees' reports help editors assess significance and identify technical issues; editors regard it essential that technical failings noted by referees are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee conflict-of-interest and confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential referees must disclose any professional and commercial competing interests before reviewing, and must not copy papers or circulate them to un-named colleagues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature requires disclosure of competing interests; editors are not responsible for referees' conduct but expect compliance with these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer suggestions and exclusion requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature welcomes authors' suggestions for suitable independent referees, but editors are free to decide who to use; editors will normally honour requests that a paper not be sent to one or two (but no more) competing groups for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may refuse to consult new referees in appeals unless there is a demonstrated technical lack or bias; editors prefer original referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature uses a transparent peer review system: for manuscripts submitted from February 2020, Nature can publish reviewer comments to authors and author rebuttal letters of published original research articles (authors may opt out).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review files are published online as supplementary peer review files; they will not contain editor discussions, editorial decision letters, or confidential comments to editors or from authors. Scheme applies only to original research Articles, not Review articles or other content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer acknowledgement and naming policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer-reviewed content will carry an anonymous statement of peer reviewer acknowledgement. For reviewers who consent, Nature will publish their names; names appear in alphabetical order and are not linked to reports unless reviewers choose to sign their comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no reviewers agree to be named, Nature will acknowledge anonymous reviewers with a standard statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed and turnaround expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature aims to make decisions rapidly: authors are usually informed within a week if the paper is not being considered; most referees deliver reports within two weeks or other agreed time limit; editors decide rapidly after receipt of reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature handles manuscripts electronically and offers advance online publication to many manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision outcomes and revision expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision letters offer options: accept without changes; accept in principle after revisions; defer final decision pending authors' response (often requiring further experiments); reject (with or without invitation to resubmit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If invited to resubmit, authors must ensure all referees' technical comments are satisfactorily addressed and accompany resubmission with a point-by-point response. Revised papers that do not seriously address reviewers' criticisms will not be sent back to referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to write responses to referees
rubrics_metrics.description: In replying to referees' comments, authors are advised to use language that would not cause offence when the paper is shown again to the referees, and to bear in mind that if a point was not clear to the referees/editors it is unlikely to be clear to nonspecialist readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised papers should be accompanied by a point-by-point response to all comments made by all referees; editors will check that referees’ suggestions have been implemented for accept-in-principle decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal grounds and process
rubrics_metrics.description: If Nature declines and does not suggest resubmission, appeals must be made in writing and confined to the scientific case for publication; appeals are unlikely to be prioritized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main grounds for successful appeal are identification of a specific technical or other point missed previously by referees and editors; authors must not submit elsewhere while an appeal is being considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subediting objectives after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Subediting (copyediting) ensures maximum clarity and reach by editing language for clarity and precision for those in other disciplines, giving special care to non-native English authors and summary paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subeditors ensure the paper meets length specified by the manuscript editor (including number of figures), that terminology and notation conform to Nature's house style, and that figures/tables are clear and will fit the space available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs, authors' responsibilities and single point of contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors receive edited text for approval before typesetting and then an e-proof including figures; authors should coordinate proof corrections through a single designated author (usually corresponding author), who is responsible for the accuracy of all content including names and affiliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs are cycled via an online production-tracking system; changes among co-authors should be coordinated so only one set of corrections is sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication scheduling and embargo policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are assigned to a print issue two weeks before publication and many are published online ahead of print; embargoed mailings highlight upcoming content to registered journalists six days in advance of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may discuss their paper with the media from six days before publication and must abide by Nature Research's embargo policies. Content of press release mailing and papers is embargoed until 1600 London time / 1100 US Eastern Time on publication day. Press office informs institutional PIOs before publication.
